headline: How to Avoid Common Mistakes in Deck Repair
articleBody: When tackling deck repairs, it's easy to fall into some common traps that can actually make things worse or just delay the inevitable. First off, a big mistake is focusing only on the surface boards and ignoring the substructure. You might replace a few rotten planks, but if the joists or beams underneath are also compromised, you haven't really solved the problem. Another common misstep is using the wrong fasteners. Decking requires specific screws and nails that can withstand outdoor conditions and provide proper holding power; using interior-grade hardware just won't cut it. Ignoring soft or spongy areas is also a huge no-no, as these often signal hidden decay that needs immediate attention. Finally, a lot of folks overlook the importance of checking for proper water drainage, which is often the root cause of wood rot. To avoid these issues, always conduct a thorough inspection that goes beyond the visible surface. If you're not sure what you're looking for, or if you suspect deeper structural issues, it's really best to bring in a professional. They've got the expertise to identify these subtle problems and ensure repairs are done correctly, especially for homes in areas like Berkeley and Oakland where decks are a big part of outdoor living.
